I have never seen a day better and brighter than the day Rasulullaah ﷺ entered Madinah. I also saw him the day he passed away and have never seen a day worse or darker than that day."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.1 Pg.234). (3)lbnSa'd(Voi.3Pg.374).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.346). Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.319) has reported a similar narration in brief.

paras: Hadhrat Anas Si reports that when the consultative assembly (appointed by Hadhrat Umar (RA) before his death) assembled, Hadhrat Abu Talha (RA) saw what they were doing (each one wishing the Khilaafah for the next) and said, "More than my fear that you should all be aspiring for the Khilaafah is my fear that you should all want to pass it on another. By Allaah! Every Muslim home has suffered a deficiency in its religious and worldly affairs by the death of Umar.

Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) narrates that they were six Muslims with Rasulullaah ﷺ when the Mushrikeen said (to Rasulullaah ﷺ), "Drive these people away from you." They then went on to belittle these Sahabah is (indicating that they as wealthy people could not sit with these poor men). The Sahabah included Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi waqqaas Sffiiii, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood, a Sahabi form the Banu Hudhayl tribe, Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and two other Sahabah (RA) whose names the narrator had forgotten, when Rasulullaah ﷺ started to consider the request, Allaah revealed the verse: ... Do not drive away those (poor Sahabah (RA)) who call (worship) their Rabb morning and evening, seeking His pleasure... (Surah An'aam, verse 52)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that a group of the Quraysh once passed by Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was in the company of some poor Muslims such as Hadhrat Suhayb (RA), Hadhrat Bilaal (RA), Hadhrat Khabbaab and Hadhrat Ammaar (RA). The Mushrikeen said, "O Muhammad! Are you content with the likes of these men from your people? Should we become followers of these people? Are these the people upon whom Allaah has bestowed His favours? Drive them away from you for perchance we may follow you if you do so." It was then that Allaah revealed the verse: Use it (the Qur'aan) to warn those who fear that they will be gathered before their Rabb without any helper or intercessor, so that they may grow concerned. Do not drive away those (poor Sahabah (RA)) who call (worship) their Rabb morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. You are not accountable at all for them (for their inner condition), nor are they at all accountable (responsible) for you, (there is therefore no reason) that (permits) you (to) drive them away and to (thereby) become of the wrong-doers (by doing this). (Surah An'aam, verses 51,52)
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.346).

paras: Discussing the verse j, Hadhrat Anas (RA) says that Hadhrat Ibn Umm Maktoom (who was blind) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ while Rasulullaah ﷺ was speaking to Ubay bin Khalaf was one of the leaders of the Quraysh and Rasulullaah ﷺ was inviting him to Islaam). When Rasulullaah ignored Hadhrat Ibn Umm Maktoom (RA) (thinking that he could always see to him later), Allaah revealed the verses: He (Rasulullaah ﷺ frowned and turned away because a blind man came to him. . . (Surah Abas, verses l ,2) After this, Rasulullaah ﷺ always honoured Hadhrat Ibn Umm Maktoom Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that the Surah was revealed with reference to the blind Sahabi Hadhrat Ibn Umm Maktoom (RA) who once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "Guide me." Because Rasulullaah ﷺ was busy speaking (giving Da'wah) to one of the leaders of the Mushrikeen, he ignored Hadhrat Ibn Umm Maktoom (RA). Devoting his attention to the Mushrik instead, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "Do you see anything wrong in what I have told you?" The man admitted that he saw nothing wrong with it. It was on this occasion that Allaah revealed the Surah: sit. S * i. t He (Rasulullaah ﷺ) frowned and turned away because a blind man came to him... (Surah Abas, verses 1,2)
sources: Surah Abas, verse 1.

paras: Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once in the company of some poor Muslims, amongst whom were Hadhrat Ammaar Hadhrat Suhayb (RA), Hadhrat Bilaal (RA) and Hadhrat Khabbaab bin Arat. Just then Aqra bin Haabis Tameemi and Uyaynah bin Hisn Fazaari arrived. The two of them held these Sahabah (RA) in low esteem and took Rasulullaah ﷺ aside saying, "We feel embarrassed that the Arab delegations will be coming to see you and will see us sitting with these slaves. Therefore, when we come to you, you should get them to leave." When Rasulullaah ﷺ agreed to do so, the two men asked to have it in writing. Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for a paper and called Hadhrat Ali (RA) to write. The poor Sahabah (RA) were still sitting there in a corner when Hadhrat Jibra'eel descended with the verses: at oj ct at ^ ot Do not drive away those Sahabah (RA) who call (worship) their Rabb morning and evening, seeking His pleasure. You are not accountable at all for them (for their inner condition), nor are they at all accountable (responsible) for you, (there is therefore no reason) that (permits) you (to) drive them away and to (thereby) become of the wrong-doers (by doing this). In this manner (as these people do not wish to associate with those of lower social standing) We use some (people) to test others so that they (the upper class) say, "Are these (lower classes) the ones whom Allaah has blessed from among us (by guiding them to Islaam instead of us)?" Allaah knows well who the grateful ones are (and it is them who Allaah shall guide to the straight path regardless of their social standing). When those who believe in Our Aayaat come to you, then say to them, "Peace be upon you. Your Rabb has made mercy (towards you) compulsory upon Himself. The (lj Abu Ya'la, lbn Jareer and Tirmidhi, as quoted in (he Tafseerof ibn Katheer. fact is that whichever one of you sins out of ignorance and then repents and (makes) amends (for his sin), (he should remember that)
Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful (Allaah will therefore forgive him)." (Surah An'aarn, verses 52-54)

Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) related further, he says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then threw the paper away and called' for us. When we came to him, he said,' - Peace be upon you'. We then drew so close to him that our knees touched his. it was the practice of Rasulullaah ﷺ when he sat with us to stand up and go when he needed to leave. However, Allaah then revealed the verse; Juu iS £" jf Rasulullaah ﷺ Restrain yourself with (in the company of) those who, seeking His pleasure, call to (worship) their Rabb morning and evening and do not shift your attention from them.' Kahaf, verse 28) Thereafter, whenever we sat with Rasulullaah ﷺ and it reached the hour when he would usually get up to leave, we would stand up and leave him. Had we not done this, he would restrain himself as long as we did not stand."
sources: All sins are committed out of ignorance because no person will sin if he really knows the punishment for the sin.

paras: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) narrates that there came to Rasulullaah ﷺ some people (new Muslims) whose hearts Rasulullaah ﷺ was still winning over to Islaam. Amongst them was the likes. of Uyaynah bin Hisn and Aqra bin Haabis. They said, "O Rasulullaah ill?! Why don't you sit at the front of the Masjid and keep away from us these people and the odour of their cloaks." They were referring to the likes of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and other poor Muslims who wore woollen cloaks because they could afford no better (they could not afford finer material and therefore perspired with the thick wool). "If you do this," they continued, "we could sit with you, discuss with you and learn from you." it was then that Allaah revealed the verses: Tj 4-f?j Oj oU-Ai (tvta oil ij ^ y go j Rasulullaah ﷺ 'Recite (to people) what (revelation) has been revealed to you from the Book of your Rabb ftf?e Qur'aan). There is none who can alter His words (Allaah's words in the Qur'aan and His promises) and you will certainly not find another place of refuge besides with Him. Restrain yourself with (in the company of) those who, seeking His pleasure, call to (worship) their Rabb morning and evening (even though they are poor and of low social standing). (Even though the wealthy ones insist that you drive these Mu'mineen away so that they can draw close to you,) Do not shift your attention from them (from the poor Mu'mineen) with the intention of acquiring the adornment of this worldly life (with the intention that if the wealthy Kuffaar accept Islaam, the status and financial strength of Islaam will grow). (Therefore,) Do not obey him (the wealthy Kaafir) whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who pursues his passions and whose (every) affair entails transgressing (the laws of Allaah). Speak the truth that comes from your Rabb. Whoever is willing, should accept Imaan (and be successful in both worlds) and whoever is willing should commit kufr (and thus suffer eternal punishment). We have surely prepared for the oppressors (the Kuffaar) a Fire, the walls of which will surround them (from all sides, making it impossible to escape).' (Surah Kahaf, verses.27,28)

These verses threaten people with the fire of Jahannam. Rasulullaah ﷺ then stood up to look for the poor Muslims and found them engaged in Dhikr at the back of the Masjid. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "All praises belong to Allaah Who has commanded me before my death to restrain myself in the company of a certain group from my Ummah.Withyou people shall I live and amongst you shall I die."

Hadhrat Abu Salamah bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Qais bin Mataatiyyah once came to a gathering that included Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA), Hadhrat Suhayb Roomi and Hadhrat Bilaal Habshi (RA). He remarked, "Here (in the gathering) are the Aws and the Khazraj tribes who have stood up to assist that man (Rasulullaah ﷺ) (this I can understand because they are Arab and people of standing). However, what is the matter with these other people (these poor non- Arabs who have no social standing? Of what use are they)?" Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) stood up and grabbing Ibn Mataatiyyah by the collar, brought him to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) reported the statement, Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up in anger and pulling his shawl along, he entered the Masjid. The announcement "Gather for salaah" was made (to assemble the people) and after duly praising Allaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O people! Verily your Rabb is but One Rabb, your father (Aadam) is but one father and your Deen is but one Deen. Take note that Arabic is neither your father nor your mother. It is merely a language and whoever speaks Arabic is therefore Arab."
(1 ! Abu Nu'aym in his (Vol.1 Pg.345).

Still holding on to the collar of Ibn Mataatiyyah, Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ What is your instruction concerning this Munaafl?Q" "Leave him to the Fire of Jahannam!" replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. ibn Mataatiyyah was therefore amongst those who left the fold of Islaam and was killed in this condition.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.46).

paras: Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that a man once came to- Rasulullaah ﷺ and asked, "O Rasulullaah ilil! I have carried my mother a distance of two on my neck over sands so scorching that a piece of meat would cook on it. Have I fulfilled the debt of gratitude I owe her?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "It may perhaps have paid off a single labour pain. "
sources: A distance of approximately six miles.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that someone once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ with an old man. "Who is this?" Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired. When he informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that the old man was his father, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Never walk in front of him, never sit down before him, never call him by his name and never make him the target of abuse (by swearing at another person's father, thereby inciting him to swear one's own father)."
sources: Tabraani in his Sageer. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.137) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Ghassaan Dhabi says, "I was walking with my father on rocky ground (in Madinah) when Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) met me and asked me, "Who is this?' When I informed him that it was my father, he said, 'Never walk in front of your father but walk either behind him or by his side. You should also never allow anyone to come between yourself and your father. Never walk upon your father's roof when there are no railings, for it will frighten him (to think that you may fall) and never eat a bone of meat that your father had his sights on, for he may be desiring to have it."
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg. 137) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ seeking permission to fight in Jihaad, Rasulullaah gpsgr asked, "Are your parents alive?" When the man replied in the affirmative, Rasulullaah said, "Then your Jihaad Is to be with them."
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim, Abu Davvood, Tirmidhi and Nasa'ee.

paras: Another narration states that a man came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "1 pledge at your hand my allegiance to migrate and to wage Jihaad seeking rewards from Allaah," "Are any of your parents alive?" Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired. "Yes," the man replied, "in fact, they are both living." "Do you want rewards from Allaah?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "Yes," the man replied. Rasulullaah ﷺ then told him, "Then return to your parents and be good to them."

Yet another narration quotes that the man said, "While I have come to you to make a pledge to migrate, I have left my parents in tears." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Return to them and make them laugh just as you have made them weep."

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) reports that when a man from Yemen migrated to Rasulullaah ﷺ (in Madinah), Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, "Do you still have any family in Yemen?" "I have my parents," he replied. "Did they permit you (to come here)?" Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired further. "No," was the reply. Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Return to them and seek their permission. You may proceed in Jihaad only if they permit you, otherwise (remain behind and) be good to them."
sources: Muslim.
Abu Dawood.
Abu Dawood.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man once said to Rasulullaah ii!?, "While I desire to march in Jihaad, I do not have the means." Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Are any of your parents still alive?" The man replied that his mother was still living. "Then," said Rasulullaah ﷺ, "meet Allaah while involved in serving her. If you do this, you will be (rewarded like) one who has performed Hajj, Umrah and waged Jihaad."
sources: Abu Ya'la and Tabraani, .is quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.4 Pg.93).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) narrates that once Rasulullaah ﷺ announced, "Prepare to march on the town with oppressive inhabitants because if Allaah wills, He will allow you to conquer it." Rasulullaah ﷺ was referring to the (Jewish) town of Khaybar. Rasulullaah ﷺ added, "No one with stubborn or frail animals should march with us." Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) then went to his mother and said, "Prepare my Journey's provisions because Rasulullaah ﷺ has just given the instruction to fight in Jihaad." His mother said, "You are leaving when you know that I am unable to enter without you by my side?" "But I cannot stay behind Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) explained. His mother then indicated towards her breasts and pleaded with him to listen to her on account of the milk that she fed him. (He however remained adamant.) She then secretly went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and stated her case before him. Rasulullaah ﷺ reassured her saying, 'You may go. Your case will be attended to without you having to come." When Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) came to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ turned away from him. Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Your turning away from me must be on account of some news that had reached you about me." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'You are the one whose mother had to indicate towards her breasts and plead with you to listen to her on account of the milk that she fed you (but you still would not accede)' Do you people think that you are not in the path of Allaah when you are with one or both of your parents? You are definitely in the path of Allaah when you treat them well and fulfil their rights." Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah then remained with his mother and was unable to fight any battles for two years until his mother passed away. The narration still continues further.

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was in Siqaayah when a woman came to him with her son. She said, "This son of mine wants to march in Jihaad but I am refusing to allow him." Rasulullaah ﷺ said (to the son), "Remain with your mother until she permits you or until death claims her life because this will earn you greater rewards."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.323) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration states that a man came with his mother to Rasulullaah ﷺ

While he wanted to proceed in Jihaad, she was averse to the idea. Rasulullaah advised him saying, "Stay glued to your mother and your reward with her shall be the same as what you would receive in Jihaad,"
sources: Tabraani.

paras: Hadhrat Talha bin Mu'aawiya Sulami (RA) reports that he once approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I wish to wage Jihaad in the path of Allaah." "Is your mother alive?" Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired. When informed that she was, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Stay glued to her feet because Jannah lies there."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.322) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Jaahimah (RA) reports that when he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ to seek advice about proceeding in Jihaad, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him whether his parents were alive. When he informed Rasulullaah ﷺ that they were, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Stay glued to them because Jannah lies beneath their feet."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol. 8 Pg.138) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Jaahimah (RA) says, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ I intend fighting in Jihaad and have come to consult with you.'

'Do you have a mother?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. When I told him that I did, he said, 'Stay glued to her because Jannah lies beneath her feet.' When I repeated myself to Rasulullaah ﷺ a second and a third time on various occasions, his reply was always the same."
sources: lbnSa'd(Vol.4Pg.l7).

paras: Hadhrat Nu'aym the freed slave of Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) left for Hajj and was somewhere between Makkah and Madinah, he recognised a particular tree and sat down beneath it. He then said, "I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ beneath this tree when a young man from this valley came and stood by him. He said, 'O Rasulullaah I have come to wage Jihaad with you in the path of Allaah thereby seeking Allaah's pleasure and the home of the Aakhirah.' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked him, 'Are both your parents alive?' 'Yes,' was his reply. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Then return and be good towards them.' The man then returned whence he came from."
sources: Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol. 8 Pg.138) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) proposed for Hadhrat Ummu Kulthoom, (her father) Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "She is still too young for marriage." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Every kinship by blood or marriage shall be severed on the Day of Qiyaamah except for all my kinship by blood or marriage.' I therefore wish to establish a kinship with Rasulullaah ﷺ (by marrying your daughter)." Hadhrat Ali (RA) said to his sons Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA), "Get your uncle married (to your sister)." They remarked, "She is a woman of individuality and will choose for herself." This remark made Hadhrat Ali (RA) furious and when he stood up, Hadhrat Hasan (RA) grabbed hold of his father's clothes saying, "Dear father! I cannot bear you being detached from us (do forgive us)!" "Then get him married," Hadhrat Ali (RA) said.
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 8 Pg.296).

paras: Hadhrat (RA) bin Seereen reports that the price of a date palm reached a thousand Dirhams during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA). Hadhrat Usaama (RA) bored to the centre of a date palm and extracted the sap, which he gave his mother to eat. People asked him, "What makes you do this when you know that a date palm can fetch a price of a thousand Dirhams?" He replied, "My mother asked me for it and if I can get it, I always give her anything she asks me for."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.94).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr (RA) narrates that he once saw Rasulullaah ﷺ delivering a sermon from the pulpit when Hadhrat Husayn (RA) came out dragging a cloth around his neck. He then tripped and fell down on his face. Rasulullaah ﷺ got off the pulpit to get to him but seeing what he intended, the Sahabah (RA) picked up the child and took him to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ took the child and carried him saying, "May Allaah destroy Shaytaan! Children are surely a trial. By Allaahl (In the eagerness of helping the child) I had no idea that I had descended from the pulpit until the child was brought to me."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami Pg.155) has commented on the chain of narrators

paras: Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Hasan (RA) once came to Rasulullaah ﷺ while he was in Sajdah and climbed on his back. Rasulullaah held him and stood up. When Rasulullaah ﷺ proceeded into Ruku, the child then stood on his back. When he got up, Rasulullaah ﷺ then left the boy and he went away.
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg. 1 75) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) narrates that he once saw Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali climb on to Rasulullaah ilif's back when he was in Sajdah. Rasulullaah ﷺ did not make the boy get off (and remained in Sajdah) until the child himself decided to get down. Rasulullaah ﷺ sometimes also parted his legs so that boy could go in from one side and out the other side.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami Pg. 1 75) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Bahiy narrates that he once asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) who it was that most closely resembled Rasulullaah ﷺ . He replied, "Hasan bin Ali most closely resembled Rasulullaah iii? and he was the most beloved to Rasulullaah ﷺ. While Rasulullaah ﷺ was performing salaah, he would sometimes come and sit on Rasulullaah ilif's back. Rasulullaah ﷺ wouid then not move from his position until Hasan got off. He would then go beneath Rasulullaah ﷺ abdomen and Rasulullaah ﷺ would separate his legs for the boy to go out again."
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.l 76) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) reports that at times when Rasulullaah was in Sajdah, Hadhrat Hasan (RA) and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) would climb on his back. When the Sahabah (RA) ventured to stop them from them doing so, Rasulullaah ﷺ would indicate to them to leave the boys alone. After completing the salaah, Rasulullaah ﷺ would place them on his lap and say, "Whoever loves me should love these two." '''

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was in Sajdah, Hadhrat Hasan Si and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) would come and climb on his back. Rasulullaah ﷺ would then prolong the Sajdah. When asked why the Sajdah was prolonged, Rasulullaah ﷺ would reply, "When my two (grand) children mounted my back, I did not like to get up to quickly."
sources: Abu Ya'la and Bazzaar, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.179). The narration of Bazzaar states that Rasulullaah ﷺ would embrace the two boys after completing his salaah. Tabraani has reported a similar narration in brief.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah Si reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out of his room with (his granddaughter) Hadhrat Umaamah bint Abil Aas (RA) on his shoulders. He then proceeded to perform salaah. He put her down whenever he went into Ruku and then picked her up again whenever he stood up (from Sajdah).
sources: Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol. 9 Pg.181) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to them with Hadhrat Hasan (RA) on one shoulder and Hadhrat Husayn (RA) on the other. He was kissing the one and then the other in turn when someone asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ You seem to love them very much?" Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "Whoever loves them loves me and whoever hates them hates me."
sources: Bukhaari (Vol.2 Pg.887). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.39) has reported a similar narration.

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) once said, "I have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ suck his tongue (the tongue of Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA)) and the tongue or lips that Rasulullaah ﷺ sucked can never suffer any punishment."
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.179) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bazzaar and Ibn Maajah have reported a similar narration in brief.

paras: Hadhrat Saa'ib bin Yazeed (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once kissed Hadhrat Hasan (RA), Hadhrat Aqra bin Haabis (RA) said, "Although I have ten children of my own, I have never kissed one of them." To this Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked, "Allaah does not show mercy to those who do not show mercy towards people."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.56).

paras: Hadhrat Aswad bin Khalaf (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once picked up Hadhrat Hasan, kissed him and then turned to the Sahabah (RA) saying, "It is because of his child that a man becomes miserly (towards others), does foolish things and becomes cowardly (fearing for the welfare of his child if anything happens to him)."
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg. 1 56) has commented on the chain of narrators. ,

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was most compassionate towards his family. He had a son (ibraheem) who was being suckled by the wife of a blacksmith at one end of Madinah. We would go to see the child at times when the house was filled with smoke from the burning of Idhkhir grass (in the furnace). Rasulullaah ﷺ would then kiss the child and smell him."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.l65) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a woman once came to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) with her two little daughters. When Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) gave her three dates, the woman gave one to each child and was about to put the third one into her mouth when the girls looked at her (with craving for her date). The mother then broke the date into two parts, gave half to each girl and then left. When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived and Hadhrat Aa'isha IS narrated to him what the woman had done, he said, "Because of her deed, she shall surely enter Jannah."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Pg.44).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) reports that a woman once came to Rasulullaah to beg for food with her two sons. Rasulullaah iiif gave her three dates, one for each of them. The woman gave one to each child and they both ate theirs. They then started looking at their mother, who then broke her date into two parts, giving half to each of them. To this, Rasulullaah fill commented, "Allaah shall be merciful towards her as she has been merciful towards her sons. Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a man once came to Rasulullaah with his child. When the man hugged the child, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Are you merciful towards him?" When the man replied that he was, Rasulullaah said, "Allaah is more merciful towards you than you are towards your Child because He is the Most merciful of those who show mercy,"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Ma'rifah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal 5 Pg.44).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that a man was sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when his son arrived. The man kissed the boy and seated him on his lap. When his daughter came, he merely seated her in front of him. To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ reprimanded, "Why have you not treated them equally?"

Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Haydah (RA) reports that he once asked Rasulullaah what the rights of his neighbours were. Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "You should visit him when he falls ill, attend his funeral when he passes away, give him a loan if he asks for one and conceal his poverty (and help him in a way that no one else comes to know). You should also congratulate him if some good comes his way and sympathise with him when a calamity befalls him. Furthermore, you should not raise your building higher than his so as to obstruct the ventilation of his house and also not distress him by the aroma of your pot (when he has no food) unless you intend dishing out some of the food for him." ^ Another narration adds, "You should provide clothing for him if he has none."

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) says that he once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ that his neighbour was causing him much trouble. Rasulullaah ﷺ encouraged him to exercise patience. When he again returned with the same complaint, Rasulullaah illf gave him the same advice. When he lodged the same complaint for the third time, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Take all your belongings out on the street and whenever anyone asks you what the matter is, tell him that your neighbour is giving you trouble. He will then receive the curses of the people. Whoever believes in Allaah and the Last Day should honour his neighbour. Whoever believes in Allaah and the Last Day should honour his guest. Whoever believes in Allaah and the Last Day should either speak what is good or remain silent."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that as Rasulullaah ﷺ was once leaving for a battle, he announced, "None who has caused harm to his neighbour should accompany us today." Someone asked, "I urinated at the base of my neighbour's wall." "You will then not accompany us today," Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed.
sources: Ahmad and Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.8Pg.171) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Miqdaad bin Aswad (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once asked the Sahabah (RA), "What do you think of adultery?" They replied, "It is Haraam. Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ have forbidden it and it will remain Haraam until the Day of Qiyaamah." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to them, "The sin of committing adultery: with ten women is less severe than that of committing adultery with the neighbour's wife." Rasulullaah ﷺ the asked, "What do you think of stealing?" They replied, "Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ have forbidden it and it is therefore Haraam." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to them, "The. sin of stealing from ten homes is less severe than that of stealing from the neighbour's house."
sources: Ibn Mubaarak, Abu Ubayd in his Ghareeb, Kharaa'iti and Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul UmmaaWol.SVgAA).

paras: Hadhrat Mutarrif bin Abdullaah (RA) says, "I had always been hearing a Hadith narrated by Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) and desired to meet him (to hear the Hadith directly from him). Therefore, when I eventually met Hadhrat Abu Dharr one day, I said to him, 'O Abu Dharr! I have been hearing a Hadith that you narrate and have always wished to meet you.' He exclaimed, 'May Allaah bless your father! You have now met me, so come (tell me which Hadith it is).' I replied, 'The Hadith I heard was that Rasulullaah ﷺ once told you that Allaah loves three persons and detests three persons.'

Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) remarked, 'It never even occurs to me to. lie about what Rasulullaah ﷺ said.' I asked, then are the three persons whom Allaah loves?' He replied, 'The man who strives in the path of Allaah with steadfastness, expecting rewards only from Allaah and then fights until he is martyred. You find mention of him in Allaah's Book that is with you.' He then recited the verse: Verily Allaah loves those (Mu'mineen) who fight (the enemies of Islaam) in His path (standing) in rows (in front of the enemy with steadfastness and unity) as if they are a solid building, saff, verse 4) I asked further, 'Who else?' he replied, 'The man whose evil neighbour gives him plenty of trouble but he exercises patience until Allaah suffices for him by either life (by changing the behaviour of the neighbour) or death taking either one of them from this world)."' The Hadith still continues further. W Hadhrat Qaasim narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once passed by his son Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan (RA) who was busy arguing with his neighbour. Hadhrat Abu Bakr said to him, "Do not argue with your neighbour because while other people (with whom you argue)will go away, your neighbour will always remain where he is (and you will have to contend with him every day)."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.42).

paras: Hadhrat Rabaah bin Rabee (RA) narrates, "We were on a military expedition with Rasulullaah ﷺ who had given every three of us a camel to ride. In the desert, two persons would ride while the third drove the camel on form behind. However, in the mountains, all would dismount. Rasulullaah ﷺ once passed by us while I happened to be walking and asked, 'I see you walking, O Rabaah?' I replied, 'I have just dismounted, while my two companions have started to ride.' Rasulullaah ﷺ then passed by my two companions and made the camel sit down, the two of them dismounted and when I passed by, they said, 'Mount the camel, sit at the front and remain there until we return (to Madinah). We shall take turns to ride with you.' When I asked them why they insisted on this arrangement, they replied, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ told us that we have a righteous travel companion whom we should treat well.
sources: Khateeb in his Muttafaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.142).

paras: Hadhrat Amr bin Mikhraaq reports that when a man of prominent appearance passed by Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) as she was having a meal, she invited him (to share the meal with her) and he sat down to eat. When another man passed by, she merely gave him a piece of bread. When someone asked her the reason for this, she replied, "Rasulullaah ill instructed us to treat people according to their status."

Another narration states that when a beggar came to beg from Hadhrat Aa'isha she had a piece of bread given to him. When a man of prominence then arrived, she allowed him to sit down and share the food she was eating. When someone asked her the reason for this, she replied, "Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed us to treat people according to their status." Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) was once on a journey when she had a supper prepared for some people of the Quraysh. When a wealthy man of prominence arrived there, she had him invited. He dismounted, partook of the meal and then left. When a beggar then arrived, she had a piece of bread given to him. Someone asked, 'You instructed us to invite the rich man but had a piece of bread given to the beggar?" -Hadhrat Aa'isha replied, "it would have been inappropriate for us to treat the rich man in any manner other thanthemannerinwhichwedid.Whenthe beggar asked for something, I had someone give him something that would please him. "Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed us to treat people according to their status." The narration has already passed in which Hadhrat Ali (RA) gave a man a set of clothing and a hundred gold coins and said, " I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Treat people according to their status' and this is the status of this man in my regard."
sources: Abu Dawood, lbn Khuzaymah, Bazzaar, Abu Ya'la, Abu Nu'aym in his Mustakhraj, Bayhaqi in his Adab and Askari in his Amthaal.

Abu in his Hilya Pg.379). Allaama Zubaydi has commented on the chain of narrators in his commentary of Ihya (Vol.6 Pg.265). (3) lbn Asaakir and Abu Moosa Madeeni in his Kitaabu Istid'aail Libaas, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.3 Pg.324).
A unit of measure used during those days.

paras: Hadhrat Agharr (RA) from the Muzaynah tribe says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once gave instructions for me to have a Jareeb of dates that was with one of the Ansaar. However, when the Ansaari procrastinated, I spoke to Rasulullaah ﷺ about it. Rasulullaah ﷺ then instructed Hadhrat Abu Bakr ii to accompany me the next morning to get the dates. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) promised to meet me at the Masjid after performing the Fajr salaah. I found him where we had arranged to meet and we left. Whenever Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) saw anyone from far, he greeted him with Salaam. He then said, 'Do you not see the tremendous virtue that others are gaining over you (by beating you to greeting).
Never let anyone beat you to making Salaam.' Thereafter, whenever we saw anyone approach from a distance, we would greet him before he could greet us.

Hadhrat Zuhrah bin Khameesa (RA) narrates, "I was once riding behind Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) on the same animal. Whenever we passed by any people and greeted them with Salaam, their reply was longer than our greeting. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) remarked, 'People have been overpowering us today.'"
Another narration quotes him as saying, "People have surpassed us in great good today."
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.4 Pg,206). Bukhaari in his Adab, lbn jareer, Abu Nu'aym and Kharaa'iti have also reported the narration, as quoted in Kanzul l/mmaal (Vols Pg.52).
Bukhaari in his Adab, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.52).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) reports, "I was once riding behind Hadhrat Abu Bakr on the same animal. Whenever he passed by any people and greeted them with the words 'As Salaamu Alaykum', they replied by saying, 'As Salaamu Alaykum wa Rahmatullaah wa Barakaatuh'. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) remarked, "People have surpassed us tremendously today.
sources: as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.156).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) was once giving a lecture when he said, "Hold fast to patience because in markets that you like and those that you do not because patience is a most excellent quality. This world has certainly attracted you. It is dragging its skirt before you and has put on its dressing and adornments for you. On the other hand, the companions of Muhammad ﷺ (were so eager to earn the rewards of the Aakhirah that they) used to sit in their yards saying, 'We sit to greet with Salaam and to be greeted."
sources: Tabraani, as quoted in Targheeb wai Tarheeb (Vol.4 Pg.207). Bukhaari has reported a similar narration in his Adab (Pg.148).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) once said, "When we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ and a tree came between us (causing us to separate), we would greet each other with Salaam as soon as we rejoined."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hiiya (Vol.1 Pg.310), as quotfed in jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.141). Bukhaari has also reported the narration in his Adab (Pg.148).

paras: Hadhrat Tufayl bin Ubay bin Ka'b narrates, "I used to accompany Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar to the marketplace every morning. When we went there, he would not pass by any hawker, trader, poor person or any other person without greeting them with Salaam. When 1 went to him one day and he requested me to follow him to the marketplace, I asked, "What do you do at the marketplace when you do not make any purchases, do not enquire about any product, do not ask prices and do not even participate in the gatherings at the market? Why do we not rather sit here and talk.' Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) said, 'Dear tubby (Hadhrat Tufayl was overweight and the term was one of endearment)! We go there for the sake of Salaam, so that we may greet whoever we meet with Salaam.

Hadhrat Abu Umaamah Baahili (RA) used to greet everyone he met with Salaam. There was none who ever beat him to making Salaam except a Jew who once hid behind a pillar and then surprised him by coming out to greet him. "Shame on you, O Jew!" Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) cried out, "What made you do this?" The Jew replied, "I noticed that you are a man who greets very often so I knew that there must be great virtue in it. I therefore wished to have the virtue." Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) then said to him, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, Verily Allaah has made the Salaam a greeting for (the Muslims of) my Ummah and a security for the Kuffaar living under our (Muslim) rule.,!
sources: Tabraani. Haythami Pg.33) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ziyaad reports, "I was holding the hand of Hadhrat Abu Umaamah as he proceeded to his house. He did not pass by any Muslim, Christian, youngster or adult without saying 'Salaamun Alaykum', 'Salaamun Alaykum'. when he reached the door of his house, he turned to us and said, 'O son of my brother! Our Nabi ﷺ commanded us to make. Salaam common amongst ourselves."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hifya (Vol.6 Pg.112).

paras: Hadhrat Basheer bin Yasaar says, "None could ever beat Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar to making Salaam."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg. 1 45) .

paras: Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that someone, once came to, Rasulullaah ﷺ and greeted with the words: "jui C ". Rasulullaah iii? replied with the words: oji iU-SS iilji ". Thereafter, another Sahabi arrived and greeted with the words: ". Rasulullaah ﷺ replied with the words: ".Thereafter, a third Sahabi SSi arrived and greeted with the words: ". This time Rasulullaah ﷺ only said, "Iiii " The Sahabi asked, "O Rasulullaah When those two came, you greeted them with words better than the words you used for me." Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'You had left nothing for me (to add because you used the full greeting). Allaah says: 'When you are greeted with a greeting, then reply with a better greeting, or (at least) return (the same greeting). .' (Surah Nisaa, verse 86) I therefore returned your greeting (since there was no better reply)."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami Pg.33) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said to her, "O Aa'isha! Jibra'eel is here and he conveys Salaams to you." Hadhrat Aa'isha replied by saying, ii She was about to add to these words when Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "The Salaam ends at that." Hadhrat Jibra'eel then said, "May the mercy and blessings of Allaah be on you, 0 Ahlul Bayt (members of Rasulullaah ﷺ household)."
sources: Tabraarti in his Awsat, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.33).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) and other Sahabah (RA) narrate that when Rasulullaah once requested permission to enter the home of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted with the words: ". Although Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied by saying, (RA) ", he did so in a voice that was not audible to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted three times and each time, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) replied in a voice that was inaudible to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When Rasulullaah ﷺ turned to leave (thinking that no one was at home), Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) ran after him saying, "May my parents be sacrificed for you, 0 Rasulullaah ﷺ Every greeting of yours fell on my ears and I had replied each time in a voice that you could not hear. I did that because l wanted to get more of your Salaams and blessings (because Salaam is a du'aa for peace and blessings)." He then took Rasulullaah ﷺ into his house and served some olive oil, which Rasulullaah ﷺ ate. After eating, Rasulullaah Si? made the du'aa: "May the pious eat your food, may the angels pray for you and may fasting people end their fasts with you."
sources: Ahmad. Abu Dawood has reported a part of the narration.

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to visit the Ansaar and when he came to the locality of the Ansaar, the children of the Ansaar would gather around him. He would then make du'aa for them, pass his hand over their heads and greet them with Salaam. When Rasulullaah ﷺ arrived at the door of Hadhrat Sa'd bin Dbaadah (RA)'s house, he greeted with the words: " ili-jj ", Although Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) "eplied, he did so in a voice that was not audible to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ greeted three times and it was his practice never to greet more than three times (when seeking permission to enter He would usually enter when granted permission or leave (if no one replied after three Salaams). Rasulullaah ﷺ therefore turned to leave (thinking that no one was at home), when Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) came running after him. The rest of the narration is the same as the one above.

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Jubayr reports that Hadhrat umar (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and greeted him. Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) however did not reply to the greeting. Hadhrat Umar (RA) proceeded immediately to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and complained to him about this. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr asked Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) why he did not reply to the greeting, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) explained, "By Allaah! I did not even hear him because I was so deep in thought." "What was it that you were deliberating upon?" enquired Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) replied, "About opposing Shaytaan. He was plaguing my mind with thoughts that I do not even wish to express for all the wealth of the world. When he cast these thoughts in my heart, I said to myself, 'if only I had asked Rasulullaah ﷺ about how we could save ourselves from these thoughts of Shaytaan!'"

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, "I expressed the very concern and question to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, 'How can we save ourselves from the thoughts that Shaytaan casts within us?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'The very same thing that I told my uncle (Abu Taalib) to say on his deathbed will save you if you say the same words. He however, did not say them.", "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ I have some shocking news for you! When I passed by Uthmaan and greeted him, he did not even reply." In a more lengthy narration, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) says, "When Umar (RA) went to Abu Bakr, he said, 'O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ ! 1 have some shocking news for you! When I passed by Uthmaan and greeted him, he did not even reply.' Taking by the hand, Abu Bakr came to me and asked, 'O Uthmaan! Your brother Umar has come to me saying that when he passed you and greeted you, you did not reply. What is the reason for this?' 'But I did no such thing, O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ I defended. "You certainly did,' Umar asserted, 'By Allaah! This pride is an old tradition of you Banu Umayyah!' 'By Allaah!' I protested, 'I have no idea that you even passed by me or that you greeted me with Salaam.'

Abu Bakr 3DS2s!jg then bore me out saying, "You have spoken the truth. It appears to me that something on your mind had distracted you from realising what had happened.' 'That is indeed so,1 I confirmed. When Abu Bakr asked me what it was, I replied, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away without me asking him what it was in which the salvation of this Ummah lay. I was engrossed in this thought, startled at my negligence at this.' Abu Bakr said, 'I have asked Rasulullaah ﷺ about this and he informed me what it is.' 'What is it?' I begged to know. He replied, I posed the question to him, saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ In what does the salvation of this Ummah lay?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Whoever accepts from me the words that I offered to my uncle but which he refused, those words shall be his salvation.' The words that Rasulullaah ﷺ offered to his uncle was to testify that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that Muhammad ﷺ is the Rasul sent by Allaah (i.e. the Kalimah 'Laa ilaaha Illallaah Muhammadur Rasulullaah ijjg').
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.7 Pg.68) has commented' on the chain of narrators. Tirmidhi has reported a portion of the end, while Abu Ya'la and Tabraani have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal Pg.298).

paras: Hadhrat Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas (RA) says, "I once passed by Uthmaan bin Affaan in the Masjid and greeted him. Although he could see me clearly, he still did not reply to my greeting. I then approached Ameerul Mu'mineen umar bin Khattaab and twice asked, 'Has anything new developed in Islaam?' 'What has happened?' he asked. 'Nothing much,' I replied, 'except the fact that when I passed by Uthmaan in the Masjid and. greeted him, he did not reply even though he could clearly see me.' Umar then sent for Uthmaan and asked, 'What prevented you from replying to your brother's Salaam?' When Uthmaan denied doing such a thing and I insisted that he did, he swore that he did not while I swore that he did. When the thought struck him, Uthmaan exclaimed, 'I seek Allaah's forgiveness and return to Him! When you passed by me just now, I was engrossed in thinking about something that Rasulullaah ﷺ once said. By Allaah! Whenever I remember these words, my eyes and heart are engulfed by a veil.'"

Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) then said, "Let me tell you what it was. Rasulullaah was about to mention to us how to begin a du'aa when a Bedouin arrived and distracted him so much that he then got up (without completing what he was going to tell us). I then followed Rasulullaah ﷺ and when I feared that he would enter his room before I reached him, 1 stamped my feet hard on the ground (as I walked). Turning towards me, Rasulullaah flif asked, 'Who is that? Is that Abu ls'haa?Q' Yes, it is I, O Rasulullaah ﷺ I replied. 'What is it then?' he asked. I said, 'Nothing much except that you were about to mention to us how to begin a du'aa when that Bedouin arrived and distracted you.' 'O yes,' Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'it is the du'aa of the man of the fish (Hadhrat Yunus when he was in the belly of the fish, (the words are): 'There is no Haah but You (O Allaah). You are Pure. I have certainly been from among the wrongdoers.' Whenever a Muslim makes du'aa to Allaah with these words, Allaah will certainly accept his du'aa.'" Conveying Salaams.

Hadhrat Abul Bakhtari narrates that Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais (RA) and Hadhrat Jareer bin Abdullaah Bajali (RA) once went to see Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi. when they came to him in a fortress in a corner of Madaa'in, they greeted him with the words " iill and "ilfl Isili " ("May Allaah keep you alive"). They then asked, "Are you Salmaan Faarsi?" When he replied that he was, they asked further, "Are you the companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ "I am not sure," he replied. This put them in doubt and they said, "Perhaps you are not the person we want." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) put them at ease saying, "I am the person you want. I have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ and have been in his company. (He then said out of humility) As for the companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ, they are those who have entered Jannah with him (and I am not sure whether I shall be amongst them). What do you two want?"

The two Sahabah (RA) explained, "We have come to you from one of your brothers in Shaam." "Who is he?" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) enquired. When they informed him that it was Hadhrat Abu Dardaa Si Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) asked, "Then where is my gift that he has sent with you?" "He has not sent any gift with us," they averred. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) warned them- saying, "Fear Allaah and hand over the trust that has been given to you! None has come to me from him without a gift for me." The two reasoned with him saying, "Please do not file a case against us for this. We have much wealth with us and you may choose whatever you want from it." "But I do not want your wealth," Hadhrat Salmaan said, "All I want is the gift that he has sent with you." "By Allaah!" they swore, "He has sent us with nothing but these words: 'Amongst you is a certain man. Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ was alone with him, Rasulullaah ﷺ wanted no one else, when you go to him, do convey my Salaams to him.'" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) then said, "This was the only gift that I wanted from you. What gift can be better than Salaam, which is a blessed and pure greeting from Allaah?"
sources: Ahmad and Rooyaani, as quoted in Kanzul Umnpal (Vol.5 Pg.54).

paras: Hadhrat Jundub (RA) says, "When meeting his companions, Rasulullaah ﷺ never shook their hands until he had first greeted them with Salaam." Someone once asked Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), "I want to ask you about a Hadith of Rasulullaah Wife? Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "I shall then narrate it to you unless it is a secret." The person then asked, "Was Rasulullaah ﷺ in the habit of shaking your hands when you met him?" Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) replied, "There was never a time that I met him without him shaking my hand.
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.37) has commented oh the chain of narrators.
Daar Qutni and Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Vmmaal ^ (Vol.5 Pg.54).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once met Hadhrat Hudhayfah bin Yamaan (RA) and was going to shake his hand, Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) turned away saying, "I am in a state of impurity." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "When a Muslim meets his brother Muslim and shakes his hand, their sins are shed off just as leaves are shed off a tree."
sources: Tirmidhi (Vol.2 Pg.97).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that the Sahabah (RA) once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ Can we bow to each other (when greeting)?" "No," came the reply. They then asked, "Can we then embrace each other?" When Rasulullaah again said "No", they asked, "Can we then shake each other's hands?" This time, Rasulullaah ﷺ's reply was "Yes".
sources: Razeen, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.142).

paras: Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that someone once asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ When any of us meets his brother or his friend, can he bow to him?" "No," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. "Can he then embrace him and kiss him?" the Sahabi asked further. Again, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No." He then asked, "Can he then take his hand and shake it?" "This he may do," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ.
sources: Tirmidhi (Vol.2 Pg.97).

paras: Another narration adds that when the Sahabi asked, "Can he then embrace him and kiss him?" Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "No, unless he shas returned from a journey."
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.36),

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ was in my house when Zaid bin Haaritha arrived in Madinah. When Zaid came to meet Rasulullaah ﷺ and knocked at the door, Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up (in great excitement), dragging his clothing along with him but without wearing anything (over his upper body). By Allaah! I have never before or ever after seen Rasulullaah ﷺ like this. Rasulullaah ﷺ then embraced Zaid and kissed him."
Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "It was the practice of the Sahabah (RA) to shake hands when meeting each other and embracing when returning from a journey."

Hadhrat Hasan narrates that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) thought of one of his companions during the night, he would sigh, "Oh how long is the night!" Then after performing the Fajr salaah, he would hurry to the person and embrace him as soon as he met him.
sources: Muhaamili, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.42). Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.101).

paras: Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam, the common people as well as the leaders came to meet him. "Where is my brother?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Who is he?" the people enquired. "Abu Ubaydah," replied Hadhrat Umar SI The people said, "Here he comes." When Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) came, Hadhrat Umar (RA) descended from his animal and embraced him. The narration continues and will soon be quoted.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.34).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abu Taalib (RA) met Rasulullaah as he was returning from Khaybar. Rasulullaah ﷺ embraced him and kissed him between the eyes saying, "I don't know whether it is the arrival of Ja'far or the conquest of Khaybar that makes me happier." Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ pulled Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) towards him and embraced him.
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.42).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen reports that Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa said, "It is with these hands of mine that I pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan says further that when they then kissed Hadhrat Salamah Sail's hands, he did not stop them.
sources: Abu Ya'la, Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.42) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abu Dawood has reported a similar narration, as quoted by Iraaql (Vol.2 Pg.181).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that he kissed Rasulullaah ﷺ's hands.
sources: Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.143).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) also reports that he kissed Rasulullaah ﷺ's hands.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.42) has commented on the chain of narrators. Abu Bakr bin Muqri has reported a similar narration, as quoted by lraaqi (Vol. 2 Pg. 1 81).

paras: Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik SSi narrates that when the verses of the Qur'aan were revealed to confirm his forgiveness (for failing to participate in the expedition to Tabook), he went to Rasulullaah ﷺ and kissed his hands.
Hadhrat Zaari bin Aamir (RA) reports that when they arrived in Madinah and Rasulullaah iill was pointed out to them, they started kissing his hands and feet.(,)

Hadhrat Mazeedah Abdi (RA) reports that Hadhrat Ashaj (RA) walked up to Rasulullaah ﷺ and started kissing his hands. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to him, "Remember! You have two qualities that Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ love." He asked, "Are these natural qualities within me or have they been developed afterwards?" "No," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ, "They have been naturally instilled within you." Hadhrat Ashaj (RA) then said, "All praise is for Allaah Who has instilled within me such qualities that Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ love."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.144).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Rajaa Utaaridi says, "When I arrived in Madinah, I beheld a gathering at the centre of which a man was kissing the head of another man saying, We would have been destroyed had it not been for you.' When I enquired who the man kissing was, I was informed that he was Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab who was kissing the head of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) for fighting the renegades who had refused to pay zakaah." (Hadhrat Abu Bakr was the only one who saw the need for this when all the other Sahabah did not see its necessity.)
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg,86).

paras: Hadhrat Tameem bin Salamah reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) arrived in Shaam, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) welcomed him, shook his hand and kissed it. The two men then sat by themselves and wept. Hadhrat Tameem always maintained that kissing the hand of pious people is Sunnah.
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzui Pg.35Q),

paras: Hadhrat Yahya bin Haarith Dhimaari says, "When I met Hadhrat Waathilah bin Asqa, 1 asked, "Was it with these hands that you pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ii!?' when he confirmed that it was, I said, 'Bring them here so that I may kiss them.' He then gave me his hand and I kissed it."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, Kharaa'iti in bis Makaarimul Akhlaaq, Bayhaqi and lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzui Ummaai (Vol.5 Pg.54).

paras: Hadhrat Yunus bin Maysarah narrates' that they once went to visit an ailing Yazeed bin Aswad when Hadhrat Waathilah bin Asqa (RA) also arrived there. When he saw him, Yazeed stretched out his hand and took the hand of Hadhrat Waathilah. He then passed Hadhrat Waathilah (RA)'s hand over his face and chest because it was with that hand that Hadhrat Waathilah (RA) had pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah iii?. Hadhrat Waathilah (RA) asked, "0 Yazeed! How are your expectations of your Rabb?" "Good," replied Yazeed. Hadhrat Waathilah (RA) then said, "Glad tidings for you! I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Allaah says, 'I treat my slaves according to their expectations of Me. If their expectations are good, I treat them well and if it is bad, I shall treat them badly.m
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.138).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Razeen says, "As we were passing Rabdha, Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa was pointed out to us. I approached him and when we greeted him, he showed us his hands saying, 'It is with these hands that I pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ The palm he extended was as large as the foreleg of a camel. We then stood up and started kissing his hand."
sources: Bazzaar, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.8 Pg.40). (3) ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 5 Pg.55). Abu Dawood has also reported the narration, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.143).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Jad'aan narrates that Hadhrat Thaabit once asked Hadhrat Anas "Did you ever touch Nabi ﷺ. with your hand?" When Hadhrat Anas said that he did, Hadhrat Thaabit kissed his hand.
sources: Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.4o) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) says that he saw Hadhrat Ali (RA) kiss the hand and feet of Hadhrat Abbaas (RA). Standing Out of Respect for a Muslim.
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.138). Tirmidhi, Ahmad and Abu Dawood have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol. 6 Pg.57).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that she had not seen anyone who resembled Rasulullaah ﷺ more in his speech and mannerisms than (his daughter) Hadhrat Faatima (RA). Whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ saw her arrive, he would welcome her, stand up and kiss her. He would then take her by her hand and take her with him to sit where he had been sitting. In a like manner, whenever he went to her, she would also welcome him, stand up and kiss him. When she came to see him during his final illness, he welcomed her and kissed her. He then whispered something to her and she started weeping. Thereafter, he again whispered something to her and she started to laugh.

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates further, "I then said to some other women, 'I had always believed that this lady was superior to other women, but it appears that she is just like other women because while weeping, she suddenly started to laugh.' When I asked her what it was that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, she replied, '(If I told you) I would then be disclosing a secret.' However, after Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, she said, 'I started to weep when Rasulullaah whispered to me that he was going to pass away. I then became happy when he informed me that I would be the first of his family to meet him.
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.169). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4) has reported a similar narration. (7) ibn Sa'd (Vol.6 Pg.28).

paras: Hadhrat Hilaal (RA) (narrates from Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) who) says that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ left (their gathering), they stood up for him and would not sit until he entered his room.

Hadhrat Abu Umaamah (RA) says, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to us taking support from his staff, we stood up for him. He then said, "Do not stand up as the non-Arabs stand up in honour of each other."

Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ once came out to them, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) (may Allaah shower His mercy upon him) said, "Stand up and seek help from Rasulullaah ﷺ in your case against the hypocrite." However, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "None should stand! Allaah is the only One for Whom people ought to stand up."

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "There was none whom the Sahabah (RA) loved to see more than Rasulullaah Si! . Despite this, they would not stand up for him when they saw him because they knew that he disliked it."

Hadhrat Naafi reports from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) that Rasulullaah forbade a person from making another stand up from his place and then sitting in the same place. Therefore, whenever someone stood up from his place for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), he would not sit there.

Hadhrat Abu Khaalid Waalibi says that when Hadhrat Ali (RA) once came out to them, they stood waiting for him to go ahead. Hadhrat Ali (RA) reprimanded them saying, "Why do I see you people standing with your chests out (like soldiers)?"

Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz reports that when Hadhrat Mu'aawiya SI once came out while Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr were seated. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Aamir (RA) stood up while Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Zubayr (RA) who was the larger of the two remained sitting. Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) remarked, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that the person who likes Allaah's servants to stand up for him should prepare for himself a house in Jahannam."
sources: Bayhaqi and Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.55).

paras: Hadhrat Waathila bin Khattaab Qurashi (RA) reports that a person once entered the Masjid when Rasulullaah ﷺ was there by himself, Rasulullaah shifted from his place for the man. When someone commented that there was enough space for the man (and Rasulullaah ﷺ did not need to move), Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "It is the right of a Mu'min that his brother should shift from his place when he sees him arrive."

Hadhrat Waathila bin Asqa (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was all alone in the Masjid when a man entered. When Rasulullaah ﷺ shifted for the man, someone asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ But there is plenty of space (for him to sit. Why didyouneedto move)?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "It is the right of a Muslim." The narration has already passed in which Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) moved from his place for Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA), saying, "Come here, O Abul Hasan." Hadhrat Ali (RA) then sat between Rasulullaah ﷺ and Hadhrat Abu Bakr.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.40) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Katheer bin Murra says, "I once entered the Masjid on a Friday where I found Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee (RA) sitting in a gathering with his legs stretched out before him. When he saw me arrive, he folded his legs in and said, "Do you know why I had stretched out my legs? I did it so that some pious person should come and sit here."
sources: Under the heading "Honouring the Family" and the subheading "Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Honours Hadhrat Ali (RA) and Vacates his Place for him".

paras: Hadhrat Muhammad bin Abbaad bin Ja'far narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas once said, "The person I have the most respect for is the one with whom I am sitting." Hadhrat Ibn Abi Mulaykah reports that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas said, "The person I have the most respect for is the one with whom I am sitting, even though he steps over people's shoulders to sit with me."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.l67).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Ja'far narrates that when two men went to see Hadhrat Ali (RA), he threw a cushion to each of them. While the one man sat on the cushion, the ( 1 ) Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg. 1 44) . other sat on the ground. Addressing the man sitting on the ground, Hadhrat Ali said, "Get up and sit on the cushion because it is only a donkey who refuses hospitality."
sources: lbn Abi Shaybah and Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Xanzui Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.55).

paras: Hadhrat Umar (RA) narrates, "My daughter Hafsah was widowed when her husband Khunays bin Hudhaafah Sahmi passed away in Madinah. He was a companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ who participated in the Battle of Badr. When I met Abu Bakr, I said, 'If you agree, I would like to get you married to Hafsah the daughter of Umar.' He however gave me no reply. It was only a few days later that Rasulullaah ﷺ proposed for her and I married her to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Abu Bakr met me thereafter and said, You may have been angry with me when you proposed that I marry Hafsah and I gave no reply?1 When I confirmed that I was, he explained, 'The only thing that prevented me from giving you a reply was that I had heard Rasulullaah ﷺ make mention of (proposing for) her and I did not wish to reveal Rasulullaah ﷺ's secret. Had he not married her, I certainly would have.

Hadhrat Anas (RA) relates, "I was in Rasulullaah ﷺ's service one day and when I had completed, I thought to myself that since Nabi ﷺ is having his siesta, I may as well leave. I then saw some children playing and stood there watching them play. Rasulullaah ﷺ then came where the children were, greeted them and then called for me. He then sent me on an errand that remains in my mouth (because it was a secret). By the time I eventually reported back to Rasulullaah ﷺ (after completing the errand), I was late in returning to my mother. "What kept you up?" she enquired. When I informed her that Rasulullaah had sent me on an errand and she asked what it was, I replied, 'It is Rasulullaah ﷺ's secret.' She then said, 'Then conceal the secret of Rasulullaah I have therefore not informed a soul about the errand. (Then addressing his student Hadhrat Thaabit Banaani, Hadhrat Anas (RA) said,) If there was anyone I would tell, it would be you."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.361). Ahmad, lbn Sa'd, Bukhaari, Nasa'ee, Bayhaqi, Abu Ya'Ia and lbn Hibbaan have also reported the narration with additions, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg. 120).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that when a man once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ about his hard heartedness, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Pass your hand over the head of an orphan and feed a poor person."
sources: Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources is confirmed by Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.160).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) narrates that when a man once complained to Rasulullaah ﷺ about his hard heartedness, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Do you want your heart to be softened and your needs to be fulfilled? Have mercy on the orphan, pass your hand over his head and feed him from your food. Your heart will then be softened and your needs will be fulfilled."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami, (Vol. 8 Pg. 1 60) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Basheer bin Aqrabah Juhani (RA) relates, "On the day the Battle of Uhud was fought, I asked Rasulullaah ﷺ , 'What has happened to my father?' Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, 'He has been martyred. May Allaah shower His mercy on him.' When I started to weep, Rasulullaah ﷺ picked me up, passed his hand over my head and put me with him on his animal saying, 'Will you not like me to be your father and Aa'isha to be your mother?
sources: Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.l6l) has commented on the chain of narrators. Bukhaari has reported a similar. narration in his Taareekh, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.1 Pg.153). ibn Mandah and Ibn Asaakir have also reported the narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.146).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) had a donkey that he took along with him when travelling to Makkah. He would use the donkey to rest or when the camels grew tired. He also had with him a turban that he tied on his head the journey). As he was riding the donkey one day, a Bedouin happened to pass by. "Are you not so-and-so?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) asked. When the man confirmed that he was the person, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) gave him the donkey saying, "Ride this away." He also handed him the turban saying, "Tie this to your head." One of his companions remarked, "May Allah. forgive you! You have given him the donkey you rest upon as well as the turban you tie on your head?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) replied, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Indeed the best act of virtue is for a man to maintain good ties with those who were close to his father after his father's death.' This man's father was a close friend of (my father) Umar.
sources: Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, Muslim, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.i69).

paras: Another narration adds that someone asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), "Would_(giviflg him) two Dirhams not suffice?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar replied, "Nabi ﷺ said, 'Care for your father's associates and do not severe ties with them, otherwise Allaah shall extinguish your Noor."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.9).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Usayd Saa'idi (RA) narrates that someone once asked, "Rasulullaah ﷺ Is there any good treatment that I may give to my parents after their demise?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Certainly. Make du'aa for them, seek Allaah's forgiveness for them, fulfil promises, maintain the ties you have through them and honour their friends."
sources: Abu Dawood.

paras: Hadhrat Ziyaad bin An'am Afriqi reports that they were once at sea as soldiers during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) when their vessel joined up with that of Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob Ansaari (RA). When their lunch was served, they invited Hadhrat Abu Ayyoob (RA), who said, "You are inviting me when I am fasting. It is however, imperative for me to accept your invitation because I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Six rights are incumbent for a Muslim to fulfil towards his fellow Muslim brother. Should he neglect one of them, he has neglected an compulsory right due to his brother, (These are) He should greet him when he meets him, he should accept his invitation, he should respond to his sneeze (by saying 'Yarhamu Kallaah'), he should visit him when he falls ill, he should attend his funeral and he should give him good advice when he asks for it.'" The narration continues further.
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab. 1 34) . (4) ibn Mubaarak and Ahmad in his Zuhd, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg.66).

paras: Hadhrat Humayd bin Nu'aym narrates that when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab and Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) were once invited to a meal, they both accepted the invitation. As they were leaving, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), "Although I attended the meal, I wish that I had not." "Why is that?" Hadhrat Uthmaan Si asked. Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Because I fear that it was hosted for show."

When he was the Ameerul Mu'mineen, Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was invited when Hadhrat Mughiera bin Shu'ba (RA) got married. When Hadhrat Uthmaan Sffiife' arrived, he. said, "Although I am fasting, I wished to accept the invitation and to pray for blessings."
sources: Ahmad in his Zuhd, as Kanzul Pg.66).

paras: Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi SE once said, "When your friend, neighbour or relative who works for the state gives you a gift or invites you for a meal, you should accept (even though you doubt the legality of his earnings). (If the earnings are actually illegal) This is something you will attain without any. effort while the sin (of the unlawful earnings) will be his."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.S Pg.66).

paras: Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra (RA) says, "I was once with Ma'qal Muzani when he removed an obstacle from the road. When I later saw something else (on the road), I beat him to removing it. 'What made you do that, O son of my brother?' he enquired. I replied, 'I did something that I had seen you do.' He then remarked, 'You have done well, O son of my brother! I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Whoever removes an obstacle from the path of the Muslims shall have the rewards of a good deed recorded in his favour and whoever has even a single good deed accepted (by Allaah) shall enter Jannah."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.87).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) narrates that they were once sitting with Rasulullaah ﷺ when he sneezed. When the Sahabah (RA) responded by saying: (Yar-Hamu Kallaah'), Rasulullaah ﷺ said: "May Allaah guide you and set all your affairs right."
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.S Pg.57) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that someone once sneezed in the presence of Rasulullaah ﷺ and then asked, "what should I say, O Rasulullaah ﷺ ?" Rasulullaah iif answered, "Say (JjjuiJS)('Alhamdu The other Sahabah then asked, "What should we then say in response, O Rasulullaah ﷺ 'You should say (Yar-hamu Kallaah')," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. The man then enquired further, "How should I then respond to them, O Rasulullaah ,i8i??" Rasulullaah ﷺ then told him that he should say: "May Allaah guide you and set all your affairs right."
sources: Ahmad and Abu Ya'la. Haythami (Vol.S Pg.57) has commented on the chain of narrators. Ibn Jareer and Bayhaqi have reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.S Pg.56).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ taught us -to respond whenever someone sneezed."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.S Pg.57).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also mentioned, "Rasulullaah ﷺ taught us that whenever anyone sneezed, he should say: Co ('Alhamdu Lillaahl Rabbil Aalameen'), When he says this, those with him should say,: (llii('Yar-Hamu Kallaah'). When they then say this, he (the one who sneezed) should reply by saying: Firullaahu Li wa Lakum').".
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.8 Pg.57) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) reports that a person once sneezed next to Rasulullaah ﷺ 's room and then said, ('Alhamdu Lillaah')". To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, iiii Kallaah')". Thereafter, another person also sneezed next to Rasulullaah ﷺ's room. This person said, iliii) ('Alhamdu Lillaah Katheeran Tayyiban Mubaarakan Fee')". To this, Rasulullaah ﷺ responded by saying, "This man has superceded the other by nineteen stages."
sources: Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaa Q/ol.5 Pg.56).

paras: "('Alhamdu Lillaah')"

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when two persons sneezed in the presence of Rasulullaah ﷺ, he replied to the one and not to the other. When he was asked about this, he replied, "Whereas the one said (Jji " ('Alhamdu Lillaah'), the other did not." ® Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that two persons once sneezed in front of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the one person belonging to a nobler social class than the other. When the nobler person sneezed, he failed to say ('Alhamdu Lillaah')", because of which Rasulullaah ﷺ did not reply to his sneeze. When the other person sneezed, he said (Jjiiift " ('Alhamdu Lillaah')" and Rasulullaah therefore replied to his sneeze. The nobleman then asked, "You did not reply when I sneezed before you, but replied when he sneezed?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "He thought of Allaah when he sneezed so I thought of him. On the other hand, you forgot Allaah so I forgot you."
sources: Bukhaari, Muslim, Abu Dawood and Tirmidhi, as quoted in Jam'ul Fawaa'id (Vol.2 Pg.145).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Burdah (RA) narrates, "I once went to (my father) Abu Moosa when he was at the home of Ummu Fadhl bin Abba as. ® When I happened to sneeze, he did not reply to my sneeze but when she sneezed, he replied to her sneeze. I informed my mother about this and when he came to her, she took him to task saying, 'When my son sneezed, you did not reply to his sneeze but when that lady sneezed, you replied to her sneeze?!' Abu Moosa replied, 'I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, "When any of you sneezes and then says wbiiili) ' ('Alhamdu Lillaah'), you should reply to his sneeze. You should however not reply to his sneeze, when he does not say ('Alhamdu Lillaah').' Therefore, when my son sneezed and did not say Lillaah'), I did not reply to his sneeze. On the other hand, when the lady sneezed, she said Ci Lillaah') and replied to her sneeze.' 'You have done well,' my mother nodded in approval.

Hadhrat Makhool Azdi reports that he was once with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar in the Masjid when someone sneezed in the corner of the Masjid. To this, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, (RA) ('Yar-Hamu Kallaah') to you if you have said (jjuiiili) ('Alhamdu Lillaah')."
sources: Bukhaari in his Adab (Pg.136).

paras: Hadhrat Naafi narrates that whenever anyone replied to the sneeze of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar by saying ' ('Yar-Hamu Kallaah')', he would say: "May Allaah shower us and you with His mercy and may He forgive us and you."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.5/). Bukhaari has reported a similar narration in his Adab (Pg. 136).

paras: Hadhrat Naafi also reports that when a. man once sneezed in front of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar and said ('Alhamdu Lillaah'), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar remarked, "You have acted in a very miserly fashion!
